instructions: Put the 1/3 cup cashews in a small bowl and cover them with 1/2 cup hot water. Leave them to soften while you start the base.
Finely chop the onion. Grate the ginger and the 4 garlic cloves. Chop the tomatoes and cut the mushrooms into quarters.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft and golden at the edges. Don't rush the onions. That's where the flavor starts.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir for about 1 minute, until they smell fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, pressing them with the spoon, until they've collapsed into a thick, jammy mash.
Transfer everything into a blender and leave it to cool for a few minutes with the lid off.

Put the skillet back over medium-high heat with 1 tbsp of the oil. Add the mushrooms in one layer and sprinkle them with 1/4 tsp of the salt and the 1/2 tsp pepper. Leave them alone for 3 minutes, then stir and cook for about 4 minutes, until they're browned and the pan is dry. Transfer them to a plate.
Add the cashews and their soaking water to the blender and blend until the paste is completely smooth.
Turn the skillet down to medium low and add the last 1 tbsp oil. Add the bay leaf, cinnamon stick and cumin seeds. After about 30 seconds the seeds will sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the turmeric, Kashmiri chili powder and coriander and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the onion and tomato paste. Stand back a little. It'll spatter. Cook it for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until it's thick and you see oil shining at the edges.
Stir in 1 1/2 cups water and the last 1/2 tsp salt and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Add the 1 cup peas and the mushrooms. Cover and simmer for 5 minutes, until the peas are tender and the gravy coats a spoon.
While it simmers, warm the 4 naan in a dry pan over medium heat for about 1 minute a side.
Take the pan off the heat and fish out the bay leaf and cinnamon. Crush the kasuri methi between your palms over the pan, then stir it in with the garam masala and 2 tbsp of chopped cilantro.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: All three versions build an onion, ginger, garlic and tomato masala with turmeric, chili and coriander, then simmer mushrooms and peas in it and finish with kasuri methi and garam masala. Hebbar's Kitchen (the lead) blends the cooked onion and tomato with cashew paste for a smooth, rich gravy; Archana's Kitchen keeps the masala chunky and finishes with cream, and Ranveer Brar makes a stock from the mushroom stems. This follows the lead but browns the mushrooms longer than its 2 minutes for more flavor, and keeps the heat to mild Kashmiri chili. Archana's Kitchen shows 4435 ratings but no rating value, so it can't be compared.
